title: Utilization of Plasmonic and Photonic Crystal Nanostructures for Enhanced Micro- and Nanoparticle Manipulation
protocol: Evaporate gold on a glass coverslip to a thickness of 20 nm using chromium as the adhesion layer.
Expose the gold-coated substrate to a mixture of EDC, latex sphere suspension, and de-ionized water for one hour to self-assemble a polystyrene sphere monolayer.
Wash away non-absorbed spheres with copious amounts of water.
Allow the formed monolayer to air dry.
Evaporate another 20 nm of gold on the latex sphere monolayer to form the random gold nanoparticle array.
Obtain 3T3 mouse cell nuclei tagged with Acridine Orange dye from the Tewari group at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center.
Add 10% bovine serum albumin (BSA) in phosphate buffered saline (PBS) to the mouse cell nuclei in a concentration of approximately 1:10 (BSA : Mouse Cell Nuclei).
Deposit 5 μL of the solution onto an aluminum grating array coverslip.
Position two stacks of two 1" by 1" coverslips to support a fifth coverslip for viewing the sample.
Place the sample under the microscope for viewing.
Construct optical tweezers by sending a 35 mW helium neon laser through a Zeiss Axio Imager.D1M equipped with a GFP 17 filter set modified for 633 nm laser radiation.
Use a Zeiss LD EC Epiplan - NEOFLAR 50x objective to image cell nuclei approximately 5 microns in diameter.
Focus the microscope on the gold nanoparticle array or diffraction grating when the sample is placed under the objective.
Translate the microscope vertically until focus is achieved on the desired nuclei.
Position the laser trap spot over a particle.
The particle should maintain its position in the laser spot even when the stage is translated.
